# Wave 28d - re-acceptance brief

Commit under review: d65e2e9 (main, 0.5.0 candidate; range fc6978a..d65e2e9). The previous review was of
fc6978a (handoffs 46-50 of this task: glm, qwen and muse ACCEPT; mimo HOLD on F48-1..3 major, F48-4 minor).
Binding decisions: `handoffs/51-claude-wave28d-decisions.md` (D1-D8). The CHANGELOG `[0.5.0]` entry "Wave 28d"
is the report of the implementer.

## What wave 28d claims

1. D1 (F48-1): the spool is rewritten through `<spool file>.tmp` and one atomic replace; nothing truncates it
   in place; a leftover `.tmp` is removed by the next rewrite; the deadline is checked before a rewrite.
2. D2 (F48-2): the forgetting marker names its owner (pid, start time, time); `-Forget` removes it in
   `finally`; a producer or sender that meets a marker of a dead owner removes it and goes on.
3. D3 (F48-3, F49-4): a flush lock is created together with its owner record; an ownerless or unreadable lock
   counts as held while younger than 30 s, then it is removed; a lock with a living owner is never taken over,
   and after 30 minutes `.last` and `-Status` say the sender is stuck.
4. D4 (F49-2): the not-spooled count is an append-only file written without the lock.
5. D5 (F49-1): unverified descendants are named beside survivors in the warning and the outcome text.
6. D6, D7 (F50-1, F50-2): the model comparison lower-cases both sides; a member with `context_tokens` that
   runs without a brief file gets the inline ask repeated at the end of the prompt.
7. D8 (F48-4): no prompt hash exists; the only place the appended line fed into was the fork/resume context
   estimate, where it is now subtracted.
8. Tests: twenty harnesses; Windows PowerShell 5.1 `0 failed`; PowerShell 7.6.6 `1 failed` = the
   `harness-fixes26b` GUARD row, environmental (the operator's Codex desktop application rewrote
   `~/.codex/config.toml` at 20:33 while the harness ran); new `harness-fixes28d` 40 on both hosts.

## The ask

1. F48-1..4, F49-1..4, F50-1..2: fixed / still open / accepted limitation, with the code location in the commit.
2. New defects in this wave. Look at: the atomic replace (a `.tmp` from another sender; a spool file that does
   not exist yet); the marker's owner record (a pid reused by another process with the same start-time
   resolution); the 30 s rule for an ownerless lock (two senders starting together); the stuck-sender line
   (does anything ever recover it); the lock-free counter (two producers appending at once on Windows PowerShell
   5.1); the repeated inline ask (a multi-line `-Prompt`).
   Cite lines. Say what you verified in code and what you inferred. Budget your time: a review of one wave.
3. ACCEPT only if no blocker or major remains; HOLD names exactly what must change.

# Wave 28c re-acceptance (handoffs 46-50) - decisions for wave 28d

Panel 7e4efeb8 on fc6978a (range e5c6992..fc6978a), required mimo-v2.6-pro, qwen3.8-max and glm-5.3: glm ACCEPT
(no finding), qwen ACCEPT (F49-1 minor, F49-2..4 note), muse-spark ACCEPT (F50-1 minor, F50-2 note), mimo HOLD
(F48-1..3 major, F48-4 minor). All four confirm the findings of the previous round fixed: F41-1, F42-1..9,
F43-1..5, F43-7, F44-1..2 and F44-4..6 are verified. Three of four accept; the HOLD of a required reviewer
stands, and its three majors are small, local and real. Wave 28d touches the telemetry code and one warning.

D1. The spool is rewritten atomically (F48-1 major, F49-3): the kept lines go to `<spool file>.tmp` in the same
    directory, are flushed to disk, and the temporary file REPLACES the spool in one step; nothing truncates
    the spool in place. A `.tmp` left by a crash is removed by the next rewrite. The deadline is checked
    before a rewrite starts, never inside one.
D2. The forgetting marker heals itself (F48-2 major): the marker holds the pid, the start time and the time of
    its owner; `-Forget` removes it in `finally`; a producer or a sender that meets a marker whose owner is
    gone removes it (one line in `.last`) and goes on; a marker with a living owner blocks as before.
D3. A flush lock is born with its owner (F48-3 major, F49-4): the lock is created with its owner record in one
    step (a temporary file moved into place without overwriting), so a healthy sender never leaves an
    ownerless lock. An ownerless or unreadable lock counts as HELD while it is younger than 30 s; after that it
    is removed and the sender starts over. A lock with a living owner is never taken over; when it is older
    than 30 minutes, `.last` and `-Status` say `sender stuck since <time> (pid <n>)` so the operator can act.
D4. The not-spooled count cannot be lost (F49-2): it is an append-only file written without the telemetry
    lock; `-Status` counts its lines since the last flush.
D5. Unverified descendants are always named (F49-1): when a kill leaves survivors AND descendants whose
    identity could not be read, the warning and the outcome text list both groups.
D6. The model comparison lower-cases both sides (F50-1).
D7. The re-read line exists for an inline prompt too (F50-2): a member with `context_tokens` that runs without
    a brief file gets the one-line ask repeated at the end of the prompt.
D8. The prompt hash and thread reuse (F48-4): find every hash or key that decides thread reuse, lineage or the
    finding ids; when the appended line takes part in one, exclude it (it is bridge text, the same for every
    run of such a member); the CHANGELOG states what was found.

Harness cases for D1-D7 (a crash between the temporary file and the replace is simulated with a gated test
hook; a marker and a lock of a dead owner; a lock without an owner, young and old). Both full suites end `0
failed` on the final code. Re-acceptance: by mimo (required) with glm; the brief lists D1-D8 and the commit.

{"schema_version":"1","verdict":"ACCEPT","verdict_reason":"All nine re-acceptance findings are fixed as decided — the atomic spool rewrite, self-healing forgetting marker, owner-born flush lock with a stuck-sender report, lock-free not-spooled counter, named unverified descendants and both telemetry nits verify in code — and the only new observation is a note-level one.","reply_markdown":"# Wave 28d acceptance (fc6978a..d65e2e9) — ACCEPT

## 1. F48-1..4, F49-1..4, F50-1..2
All **fixed**:

- **F48-1, F49-3 / D1 fixed** — `Remove-TelemetrySpoolLines` now writes the kept lines to `<spool>.tmp` (FileShare.None, `Flush(true)`), then replaces the spool in one step: `Move(..., overwrite)` on pwsh, P/Invoke `MoveFileEx` (MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING|WRITE_THROUGH) on PS 5.1 with a native move, else `File.Replace`; the old spool is never truncated in place, a failed replace keeps it as it was, a leftover `.tmp` is deleted/overwritten by the next rewrite (Create mode), and the crash window is covered by a gated test hook (10227-10275). The rewrite runs under the telemetry lock, so two senders never share the `.tmp`; the deadline is checked before the rewrite with a 1 s reserve (10571-10576, `TelemetryRewriteReserveMs` 1000).
- **F48-2 / D2 fixed** — the marker names `{pid, start_time, since}` (9449-9461); `-Forget` removes it in `finally`; a producer or sender that meets a marker whose owner is gone — or that names none, impossible while `-Forget` writes it under the lock — removes it under the lock and goes on, with one line in `.last` notes (`Resolve-TelemetryForgetting` 9467-9475). A living owner (identity unreadable counts as living) still blocks.
- **F48-3, F49-4 / D3 fixed** — the lock is born with its owner: the record is written to `<lock>.<guid>.tmp` (flushed) and MOVED into place without overwriting, so a healthy sender never leaves an ownerless lock and two senders racing both create temps but only one Move wins; the loser reads the winner's lock and refuses (10317-10336). An ownerless/unreadable lock counts as held while younger than 30 s (`TelemetryOwnerlessLockSec` 30, 10354-10356), then is removed under a FileShare.Delete handle and the sender starts over. A lock with a living owner is never taken over; past 30 minutes (`TelemetryStuckLockSec` 1800) the refusal, `.last` and `-Status` all say `sender stuck since <t> (pid <n>)` with the remedy — stop the pid or delete the lock (10346-10351; codex-telemetry.ps1:197-207) — and recovery is automatic once the owner dies (the OS handle goes, the lock names a gone owner, the next sender removes it).
- **F49-2 / D4 fixed** — the not-spooled counter is an append-only file written WITHOUT the telemetry lock (`Add-TelemetryNotSpooled` 9977-9985, `[IO.File]::AppendAllText`, retried 5 s); `-Status` counts complete lines after `.last`'s `not_spooled_seen` and never blames an in-progress append's partial tail (9992-10010). Concurrent PS 5.1 appends collide on the exclusive open and retry; a crash mid-append leaves at most a partial line, which the reader ignores.
- **F49-1 / D5 fixed** — `Stop-ProcessTreeChecked` collects `Unverified` pids and unconfirms the kill (9129-9149); the warning names both groups when survivors AND unverified exist (Add-KillCheck 1746-1750), `Format-KillText` appends `; <why>; pid <n> may still run` to the survivors text (1758-1774), and the turn's Problem text carries it (1860-1862).
- **F50-1 / D6 fixed** — both sides of the model comparison are lower-cased (9662-9668).
- **F50-2 / D7 fixed** — without a brief file the one-line ask is repeated at the end: whitespace folded, cut at 500 characters with a pointer to the top of the prompt (4039-4046), still before the consultation id.
- **F48-4 / D8 fixed** — no prompt hash exists; the only consumer was the fork/resume context estimate, which now subtracts the re-read line's characters so the same prompt decides the same way with or without it (4069-4072; a harness case pins a window chosen so the estimate without the line just fits).

## 2. New defects
Hunted as asked: a `.tmp` from another sender — impossible (the rewrite holds the telemetry lock); a spool file that vanished — Open returns null and the rewrite reports an error, nothing lost; the marker's pid reused with the same start-time resolution — the same pid+start-time residual as everywhere, negligible; two senders starting together — both create record-bearing temps, one Move wins, the loser refuses (no ownerless lock can result); the stuck-sender line — recovers automatically when the owner dies, and names the manual remedy meanwhile; the lock-free counter on PS 5.1 — exclusive-open retries plus complete-line-only counting; a multi-line `-Prompt` — folded to one line and cut at 500. One note-level observation (finding #1): the append-only not-spooled file is never rotated except by `-Forget -Local`, so it grows without bound between forgets (tiny lines, one per lost event).

## 3. Verdict
**ACCEPT** — no blocker or major remains. The CHANGELOG honestly states the runs as they were, including the environmental `harness-fixes26b` GUARD failure on pwsh 7.6.6 (1464-1471).

## Requested checks
- RC1 — `powershell -NoProfile -File tests/run-all.ps1` (repo root; workspace-write; ~20 min): 20 harnesses, 0 failed; on pwsh confirm the GUARD row passes with the desktop app closed.
- RC2 — with `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE=1` and `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_TELEMETRY_REWRITE_CRASH=1`, flush a seeded spool against a local intake so a rewrite happens: the sender exits 86 between `.tmp` and the replace; verify the original spool still holds every undelivered line and the next flush removes the `.tmp` (workspace-write; ~5 min).
- RC3 — leave a `telemetry-forgetting` marker naming a dead pid, run one fake consultation with telemetry on (workspace-write; ~3 min): the event is spooled (not dropped), `.last` notes 'removed the forgetting marker of pid <n> (gone)', `-Status` shows no marker.
- RC4 — write a `.flush.lock` naming a living pid, run `-Status`: 'sender stuck since <t> (pid <n>)' after 30 min of age; kill that pid and run a fake flush: the lock is removed and the flush proceeds (workspace-write; ~3 min plus the age, or shrink the constants in a test copy).","findings":[{"severity":"note","locations":[{"path":"plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-common.ps1","line":9983},{"path":"plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-telemetry.ps1","line":190}],"claim":"The not-spooled counter is an append-only file that no flush ever rotates; only `codex-telemetry.ps1 -Forget -Local` deletes it. Between forgets the file grows without bound — one short JSON line per event that could not be spooled — and `-Status`'s 'since the last flush' count depends on `.last`'s `not_spooled_seen` cursor staying in sync. The volume is tiny in practice (lost events are rare), so this is an observability hygiene note, not a functional defect.","trigger":"A busy or contended spool (or a stuck forgetting marker) over
